"GRAVEBORN: The First Descent
Create a fully playable, single-player, 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG titled GRAVEBORN: The First Descent.
VISUAL STYLE AND ATMOSPHERE
Build a grim medieval fantasy world with detailed low-poly 3D environments, realistic shadows, atmospheric fog, torchlight, ruined stone structures, and oppressive gothic architecture.
The aesthetic should feel grounded, mature, and dangerous. Use desaturated earth tones, worn iron armor, weathered leather, decaying vegetation, and ancient crypts. Avoid bright cartoon graphics.
Use a smooth isometric camera that can zoom and rotate around the environment.
EXPLORATION
Players control a small mercenary company from an elevated third-person/isometric perspective.
Create one small explorable overworld area containing:
- An abandoned mercenary camp.
- A winding forest path.
- Ancient grave markers and ruined structures.
- A crypt entrance leading underground.
Allow players to move their party by clicking or tapping destinations. The party should travel together.
Approaching enemies initiates a tactical battle on a separate 3D battlefield.
PLAYER PARTY
Create two playable characters:
1. Vanguard — Melee Fighter
- 12 HP
- 3 attack damage
- Movement allowance: 4 tiles
- Melee attack range: 1 tile
- Ability: Shield Bash, dealing 2 damage and pushing an enemy backward one tile.
2. Occultist — Dark Magic Caster
- 8 HP
- 2 attack damage
- Movement allowance: 3 tiles
- Magic attack range: 3 tiles
- Ability: Grave Touch, dealing 3 damage at close range.
- Ability: Revive, restoring 3 HP to a downed ally once per battle.
Display each character as an animated 3D model with visible equipment and health bars.
TACTICAL COMBAT SYSTEM
Implement an authentic turn-based tactical combat system with a visible square movement grid.
Combat rules:
- Player characters act first, in any order.
- Each character receives one movement allowance and one primary action per round.
- Movement and actions are separate resources.
- Characters may attack before or after moving.
- Highlight reachable tiles when selecting movement.
- Highlight valid enemy targets when selecting an attack.
- Prevent actions outside available movement or attack range.
- Prevent movement through occupied tiles and solid obstacles.
- Once both characters finish their turns, enemies take their turns.
- After all enemies act, begin a new round.
- Display the active round, selected character, movement remaining, and primary action status.
ENEMIES AND AI
Create three enemy types:
Shambling Undead
- 6 HP
- 2 melee damage
- Movement: 2 tiles
Skeleton Archer
- 4 HP
- 2 ranged damage
- Movement: 3 tiles
- Attack range: 4 tiles
Grave Warden — Boss
- 18 HP
- 4 melee damage
- Movement: 2 tiles
- Special attack: Grave Cleave, damaging all adjacent enemies.
Enemies should intelligently approach party members, avoid obstacles, and attack valid targets. Archers should attempt to maintain distance.
DOWNED, REVIVE, AND DEATH
Characters reduced to 0 HP become downed instead of immediately dying.
Downed characters cannot move or attack. The Occultist may revive a downed ally once per battle using a primary action while adjacent.
If both party members are downed, display a defeat screen with a restart option.
LEVEL DESIGN AND GAMEPLAY LOOP
Create a complete 5–10 minute adventure:
1. Begin at the mercenary camp.
2. Explore a short forest path.
3. Fight two Shambling Undead.
4. Continue into the ancient crypt.
5. Fight one Shambling Undead and one Skeleton Archer.
6. Enter the final chamber and battle the Grave Warden.
7. Defeat the boss to receive gold and complete the adventure.
Restore the party's HP after each victory for this prototype.
INTERFACE AND CONTROLS
Support mouse and touchscreen input.
Include:- Character selection.
- Click/tap-to-move navigation.
- Attack button.
- Ability buttons.
- End Turn button.
- Health bars.
- Movement and action indicators.
- Camera zoom and rotation controls.
-Victory, defeat, and restart screens. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## Objective
- Build a fully playable, single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG, **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, with exploration, tactical battles, and a complete adventure loop.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric zoom/rotation, forest camp, winding path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two playable heroes with specified HP, damage, movement, attacks, abilities, downed/revive rules, and health bars.
- Turn-based grid combat with movement/action resources, reach and obstacle validation, enemy AI, and three encounters ending with a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls; responsive phone/tablet UI; victory, defeat, restart screens.
- Finish the build without clarification; note assumptions briefly. Capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot for a check.

## Decisions
- No existing game framework was present; began a standalone browser implementation with Three.js from a CDN and custom HTML/CSS/JavaScript.
- Assumed an isometric-style perspective and simple procedural low-poly assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial UI and responsive styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Began procedural Three.js game implementation in `game.js`.

### Active
- `game.js` is incomplete and currently ends after `updateHeroBar`; game initialization/UI event wiring, remaining gameplay code, testing, and screenshot check are still needed.

### Blocked
- An attempted edit failed because the expected text was not found. The subsequent full replacement of `game.js` overwrote previously added gameplay sections, so they must be reimplemented.

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `game.js`: tactical battlefield, enemies, input/actions, enemy turns, progression, defeat/victory, UI wiring, animation loop, and initialization.
2. Check for syntax/runtime issues and run the game locally.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot; fix any visible problems.
4. Summarize implementation assumptions and verification results for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Visual theme and responsive layout.
- `game.js`: Partial procedural Three.js scene/game logic; currently incomplete.

## Important Context
- The last write replaced `game.js` with code ending at `updateHeroBar`; it currently has no remaining gameplay code or startup call.
- Changes are uncommitted.

17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, tactical battles, and a complete campaign loop.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D world with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two playable heroes with distinct stats, attacks, abilities, health, and downed/revive rules; grid-based turn combat with enemy AI and three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, note assumptions briefly, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone browser game with Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Assume an isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI in `index.html`, styling in `style.css`, and exploration/combat/campaign implementation in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started a local server at `http://localhost:3002`; browser successfully loaded the game and rendered its UI and 3D scene.
- Captured `screenshots/graveborn.jpg` and `screenshots/explore.jpg`.
- Tested dismissing the intro and clicking the path; the exploration event overlay appeared as expected.

### Active
- Validate and play through combat and campaign in-browser; fix any issues found.
- Review screenshots visually and confirm `screenshots/graveborn.jpg` is a useful in-game capture.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Click `DRAW STEEL →` on the current exploration event and test battle controls, turns, and enemy behavior.
2. Continue validating campaign progression and endings; fix discovered issues and rerun `node --check game.js`.
3. Inspect the screenshots, then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, battle, and campaign implementation.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Visual theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/graveborn.jpg`: Initial JPEG verification screenshot.
- `screenshots/explore.jpg`: Exploration screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Current browser state is at the first exploration event, with `DRAW STEEL →` available.
- Browser console reported a 404 for `/favicon.ico` and WebGL GPU-stall performance warnings; no gameplay runtime error was observed so far.

- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, tactical battles, and a complete campaign loop.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D world with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two playable heroes with distinct stats, attacks, abilities, health, and downed/revive rules; grid-based turn combat with enemy AI and three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, note assumptions briefly, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a standalone browser game with Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Assume an isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI in `index.html`, styling in `style.css`, and exploration/combat/campaign implementation in `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

- Inspect screenshots and confirm `screenshots/graveborn.jpg` is a useful in-game capture.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Figure out how to trigger the exploration event from the current browser state; clicking at `(545, 390)` and `(595, 440)` did not advance it.
2. Click `DRAW STEEL →` when available; test combat and continue through campaign, fixing issues found.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js`, inspect the screenshots, and summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, battle, and campaign implementation.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Visual theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/graveborn.jpg`: Initial JPEG verification screenshot.

- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, battles, and a campaign ending.

- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.

- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, battles, and a campaign ending.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, briefly note assumptions, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface, styling, exploration, tactical battles, and campaign in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Earlier `node --check game.js` passed.
- Local game loaded at `http://localhost:3002`; intro dismissal, exploration event, and transition into first battle were verified.
- Captured `screenshots/graveborn.jpg`, `screenshots/explore.jpg`, `screenshots/battle.jpg`, and `screenshots/move.jpg`.
- Verified a hero can move, spend an action, and end a turn; enemy AI completes its turn and advances to round 2.
- Updated `game.js` to exclude occupied tiles from move highlights and hide the selection prompt after a successful move.

### Active
- Validate targeting and damage feedback, remaining encounters, campaign progression, and victory/defeat endings.
- Re-test the latest movement-occupancy change and check the final game with `node --check game.js`.

### Blocked
- No confirmed blocker; reliable enemy targeting and visible damage confirmation still need verification.

## Next Move
1. Re-test movement and enemy targeting in the first battle after the latest `game.js` change; confirm enemy HP changes.
2. Exercise all three encounters, enemy turns, and campaign victory/defeat and restart flows; fix issues discovered.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, refresh the final screenshot if needed, and report assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, battle, campaign logic, raycasting, and latest movement change.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/battle.jpg`: First-battle capture.
- `screenshots/move.jpg`: Movement-selection capture.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- The browser is at `http://localhost:3002/` in the first battle, round 2; the Occultist is selected.
- Click coordinates used in earlier tests sometimes produced “That tile cannot be reached.” or “Choose a living enemy.”; one later click spent the Occultist’s action, but enemy HP change was not confirmed.

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, battles, and a campaign ending.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, briefly note assumptions, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface, styling, exploration, tactical battles, and campaign in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Earlier browser checks verified intro dismissal, exploration event, battle transition, movement, action use, enemy turn, and round advancement.
- Updated movement highlighting to exclude occupied tiles; successful movement hides the selection prompt.
- Updated attack and ability targeting to hide the prompt after a successful action; ability targeting now prompts for an enemy target.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the latest code changes.
- Captured JPEG screenshots including `screenshots/graveborn.jpg`, `screenshots/explore.jpg`, `screenshots/battle.jpg`, and `screenshots/move.jpg`.

### Active
- Reliably verify enemy targeting and confirm enemy HP changes.
- Test all three encounters, campaign progression, victory/defeat endings, and restart flows.

### Blocked
- Targeting verification is inconclusive: Playwright clicks left the Occultist showing `SPENT`, but enemy HP change was not confirmed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current battle in the browser and verify a valid target click changes an enemy’s HP.
2. Exercise all three encounters, enemy turns, campaign transitions, victory/defeat, and restart; fix discovered issues.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js`, refresh screenshots if needed, and report assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign logic, raycasting, and latest targeting/movement changes.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/battle.jpg`: Latest battle capture.
- `screenshots/move.jpg`: Movement-selection capture.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Recent Playwright snapshots showed the first battle, round 1, with Occultist moved and action spent; targeting feedback still needs a clear confirmation.
- Some earlier screen-coordinate clicks produced “That tile cannot be reached.” or “Choose a living enemy.”

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, battles, and a campaign ending.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, briefly note assumptions, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented interface, styling, exploration, tactical battles, and campaign in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Verified the first battle can be won and advances to stage two; campaign transition shows a `CONTINUE` event card.

### Active
- Continue testing encounter two and the final boss, then verify victory/defeat and restart flows.
- Confirm targeting behavior and enemy HP change in encounter two; current run advanced into encounter two but the target/action sequence used afterward is not yet confirmed.
- Re-run syntax checks and capture/refresh a final screenshot.

### Blocked
- No external blocker; remaining campaign and ending verification is incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current browser state in encounter two and verify valid target selection changes enemy HP.
2. Complete campaign testing through the boss, victory/defeat, and restart flows; adjust automation for the actual state/UI when necessary.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, refresh a representative JPEG screenshot, and report assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign progression, targeting, and endings.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/`: Existing JPEG captures, including battle and exploration states.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Earlier campaign automation timed out waiting for `/CONTINUE/`; newer checks confirmed the first victory transition does display `CONTINUE →`.
- Latest browser state is encounter two, `THE SUNKEN CRYPT`, round 1. In the latest sequence the Occultist is marked `SPENT`, but it is unclear whether an enemy target was valid; confirm HP change before assuming targeting passed.

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a playable single-player 3D dark-fantasy tactical RPG with exploration, battles, and a campaign ending.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Finish without clarification, briefly note assumptions, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented interface, styling, exploration, tactical battles, campaign progression, and endings in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Verified the first battle can be won and advances the campaign.
- In encounter two, Grave Bolt killed a Shambling Undead and gold increased from 16 to 24.
- Earlier browser checks covered intro dismissal, exploration events, movement, action use, enemy turn, and round advancement.
- Existing JPEG screenshots are in `screenshots/`, including `screenshots/graveborn.jpg`, `screenshots/explore.jpg`, `screenshots/battle.jpg`, `screenshots/move.jpg`, and `screenshots/targeting.jpg`.

### Active
- Finish encounter two and test the final boss, victory/defeat screens, and restart flow.
- Run a final syntax check and refresh a representative JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue encounter two from its current state, then proceed through the boss encounter.
2. Verify campaign victory, defeat, and restart behavior.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, capture or refresh a screenshot under `screenshots/`, and report test results and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign progression, targeting, and endings.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/`: Existing JPEG captures.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Latest browser state is encounter two, round 3: Shambling Undead slain, 24 gold, Occultist action spent, Skeleton Archer alive; Vanguard selected with movement spent and action ready. Recent attempted ability targeting clicks did not select a living enemy.
- `screenshots/` contains existing captures; a temporary screenshot was saved to `/tmp/opencode/current-crypt.jpg`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a complete playable single-player 3D tactical RPG with exploration, three connected encounters, and campaign endings.
- Improve character animations for walking, combat, casting, damage, and death.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Prioritize functional environment/navigation, party control, tactical combat/rules, AI, downed/revive mechanics, campaign progression, endings/restart, then animation and atmosphere.
- Do not implement multiplayer, open-world procedural generation, crafting, complex inventories, or recruitment.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented interface, styling, exploration, tactical battles, campaign progression, and endings in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Verified the first battle can be won and advances the campaign; previously verified Grave Bolt killed an undead in encounter two and gold increased from 16 to 24.
- Added animation helper functions in `game.js` for movement, attacks/casting, damage flash, and down/death state.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest animation-helper edits.

### Active
- Wire and verify the new animation helpers in actual character/enemy movement, combat, damage, and death updates.
- Finish encounter two and test the final boss, victory/defeat screens, and restart flow.
- Rerun syntax validation and capture a representative JPEG screenshot under `screenshots/`.

### Blocked
- Browser target-selection attempts in encounter two repeatedly returned “Choose a living enemy.”; enemy picking and target coordinates need investigation before campaign verification can continue.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and update `animate()` and battle action/movement paths to drive smooth animation states and death cleanup.
2. Resolve enemy targeting, then complete encounters two and three and test endings/restart.
3. Run `node --check game.js` and save a JPEG screenshot under `screenshots/`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign progression, animation helpers, and endings.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/`: Existing JPEG captures, including `graveborn.jpg`, `explore.jpg`, `battle.jpg`, `move.jpg`, and `targeting.jpg`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Browser is in encounter two, round 3. Vanguard has 10/12 HP; Occultist has 8/8 HP; gold is 24. The undead was slain; Skeleton Archer remains alive.
- Recent attempted attack/ability clicks did not select a living enemy. Current screenshot attempts were saved to `/tmp/opencode/current-crypt.jpg` and `/tmp/opencode/current2.jpg`.

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a complete playable single-player 3D tactical RPG with exploration, three connected encounters, campaign endings, and smooth character animations.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Prioritize environment/navigation, party control, tactical combat/rules, AI, downed/revive mechanics, campaign progression, endings/restart, then animation and atmosphere.
- Exclude multiplayer, procedural open-world generation, crafting, complex inventories, and recruitment.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented interface, exploration, tactical battles, campaign progression, and endings in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added smooth movement, attack/cast, damage-flash, enemy-death, and downed animations; wired battle actor updates and hero arm movement into `animate()`.
- Added persistent grid coordinates for enemies, animated battle and enemy movement, and improved targeting to prioritize enemy actors over tiles.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser smoke test loaded the game without page or console errors and rendered a Three.js canvas.

### Active
- Verify enemy targeting and combat in encounter two; complete encounters two and three, including victory/defeat and restart.
- Capture a representative JPEG screenshot under `screenshots/`.

### Blocked
- Full campaign verification is unfinished; encounter-two target selection still needs browser verification.

## Next Move
1. Test enemy targeting and combat in encounter two; investigate further if “Choose a living enemy.” persists.
2. Finish the second encounter and verify the Grave Warden fight, endings, and restart.
3. Save a representative JPEG screenshot under `screenshots/` and rerun `node --check game.js`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign progression, target picking, and animations.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/`: Existing JPEG captures, including `graveborn.jpg`, `explore.jpg`, `battle.jpg`, `move.jpg`, and `targeting.jpg`.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Game is served at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- A browser smoke test dismissed the intro and confirmed the title, `THE ASHEN CAMP`, and one canvas; screenshot saved temporarily at `/tmp/opencode/game-start.jpg`, not in the project’s `screenshots/` directory.

## Objective
- Build and verify **GRAVEBORN: The First Descent**, a complete playable single-player 3D tactical RPG with connected encounters, campaign endings, and smooth character animations.

## Requirements
- Grim low-poly 3D setting with isometric-style zoom/rotation, camp, forest path, grave markers, ruins, and crypt.
- Two heroes with distinct stats and abilities; grid-based combat, enemy AI, three encounters ending in a boss.
- Mouse and touch controls, responsive UI, victory/defeat and restart screens.
- Prioritize environment/navigation, party control, tactical combat/rules, AI, downed/revive mechanics, campaign progression, endings/restart, then animation and atmosphere.
- Exclude multiplayer, procedural open-world generation, crafting, complex inventories, and recruitment.

## Decisions
- Standalone browser game using Three.js from a CDN and procedural low-poly assets.
- Isometric-style perspective and simplified procedural models.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented exploration, interface, tactical battles, campaign progression, endings, and animations in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added persistent enemy grid coordinates, animated battle/enemy movement, and enemy-prioritized target picking.
- Earlier syntax and browser smoke checks passed; targeting and Grave Bolt attacks were confirmed to deal damage and grant gold for kills.
- Encounter one was reached and combat was verified using the game’s actual camera projection: kills, enemy turns/movement, party damage, and round advancement all worked.

### Active
- Verify encounter-one victory and then encounters two and three, endings, and restart.
- Rerun syntax and browser checks after campaign verification.

### Blocked
- End-to-end campaign verification remains incomplete: the latest browser automation killed both encounter-one enemies and triggered the delayed transition, but its attempt to click the now-hidden `#end-turn-btn` timed out while the UI was changing.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing from encounter-one victory; wait for its transition/event UI before interacting.
2. Verify encounters two and three, both endings, and restart.
3. Save or confirm a representative JPEG in `screenshots/`, then rerun `node --check game.js` and browser smoke checks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, exploration, combat, campaign progression, target picking, animations.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Theme and responsive layout.
- `screenshots/`: Existing exploration and battle JPEG captures.

- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
